definitions.explanation: A counter for birds and rabbits. Historically, rabbits were counted with this counter because monks could eat rabbit meat if they called them 'birds.'

examples.english: There are five birds in the garden.

examples.japanese: ⟦{一|いち}→一：00705_ichi⟧{羽|わ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦にわとり→鶏：05202_niwatori⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{卵|たまご}→卵：02222_tamago⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{産|う}みました→産む：01899_umu⟧。
⟦うさぎ→兎：01854_usagi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{三|さん}→三：00749_san⟧{羽|ば}⟦{飼|か}っています→飼う：08151_kau⟧。

⟦{昨日|きのう}→昨日：00859_kinou⟧⟦{公園|こうえん}→公園：00581_kouen⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{白|しろ}い→白い：00587_shiroi⟧⟦{鳥|とり}→鳥：00679_tori⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{六|ろっ}→六：00747_roku⟧{羽|ぱ}⟦{見|み}ました→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{今日|きょう}→今日：00496_kyou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{一|いち}→一：00705_ichi⟧{羽|わ}⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦いませんでした→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Yesterday I saw six white birds in the park, but today there wasn't even one.

notes:
{羽|わ} is the counter for birds and rabbits.

COUNTING READINGS:
- ⟦{一|いち}→一：00705_ichi⟧{羽|わ} (1)
- ⟦{二|に}→二：00736_ni⟧{羽|わ} (2)
- ⟦{三|さん}→三：00749_san⟧{羽|ば} or ⟦{三|さん}→三：00749_san⟧{羽|わ} (3)
- ⟦{四|よん}→四：00767_yon⟧{羽|わ} (4)
- ⟦{六|ろっ}→六：00747_roku⟧{羽|ぱ} (6)
- ⟦{八|はっ}→八：00698_hachi⟧{羽|ぱ} (8)
- ⟦{十|じゅっ}→十：00708_juu⟧{羽|ぱ} (10)
- ⟦{何|なん}→何：00498_nani⟧{羽|わ} (how many)

Note the sound changes: ば after ん, ぱ after っ.

ETYMOLOGY:
The origin of counting rabbits with {羽|わ} is traditionally attributed to Buddhist monks: since eating meat was forbidden, they classified rabbits as "birds" (⟦{鳥|とり}→鳥：00679_tori⟧) so they could eat them. While this folk etymology is well known, the actual origin is debated.

USAGE:
Used for all types of birds, from small songbirds to large birds like cranes. Also used for rabbits but not for other small mammals.
